physics_goals.locator: CERN Courier, "The time projection chamber turns 25"
physics_goals.quote: The PEP-4 TPC (figure 1) was built to combine charged-particle tracking with good particle identification by measuring the specific energy loss (dE/dx) of charged particles.
physics_goals.value: Combine charged-particle tracking with good particle identification by measuring dE/dx

summary.plain: The first big time projection chamber, invented at Berkeley Lab and used at SLAC's PEP ring from 1982 to 1990. It tracked charged particles in three dimensions and identified them from their ionisation, setting the pattern for later detectors at LEP and RHIC and now at the LHC.
summary.technical: PEP-4 TPC at PEP (29 GeV e⁺e⁻): 2 m long cylindrical TPC, 40 cm inner and 2 m outer diameter, argon-methane gas at 8.5 atm in a solenoid, dE/dx particle identification; first assembled fall 1981, installed in the PEP beam line January 1982, data taking from April 1982; PEP-4 and PEP-9 (Two-Gamma) merged about 1985; completed running 1990.
